BiblicalUsage: The word rishʻâh means wrong (especially moral). In Deuteronomy 9:4, we read, "…saying, For my righteousness the LORD hath brought…"; in Ezekiel 5:6, "…statutes more than the countries that round about…". You hear it again in Isaiah 9:18 — "…wickedness burneth as the fire: it shall devour…" — and in Malachi 1:4, "…will return and build the desolate places; thus…".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe rishʻâh matters because God chose this word, and it tells the truth about how God deals with his people. And I believe rishʻâh still speaks to us today, because God's word does not go out of date.
